question: How does a request travel through app.use middleware, the router and the error handler in Express 5?

glossary.definition: A function (req, res, next) registered with app.use; it runs for every request whose path starts with its mount path.
One entry of the router's stack: a path matcher plus the function to call. app.use adds a prefix-matching layer, app.get/app.route an exact-matching one that holds a route.
The router's ordered list of layers, walked from the first to the last for each request.
The handlers registered for one path with app.get, app.post and so on; it has its own small stack filtered by HTTP method.
A middleware declared with four parameters (err, req, res, next). The router only calls it while an error is pending.

glossary.definition: The callback the router calls when it runs out of layers: it answers 404 when no error is pending and an error status otherwise.
The callback each handler gets. next() moves on, next(err) switches to error mode, next('route') skips the rest of the route, next('router') leaves the router.

blocks.title: A request through Express 5
blocks.subtitle: express 5.3.0 · router 2.2.0 · finalhandler 2.1.0
blocks.answer: The app is a plain function that hands each request to one router; the router walks its stack of layers in registration order, calling each layer whose path matches. Once a handler calls next(err) or throws, the router keeps walking but calls only four-argument error handlers; when the stack runs out, finalhandler answers with 404 or the error's status.

facts.text: app(req, res) is just app.handle(req, res, next): Express itself adds no pipeline of its own.
Order is registration order: app.use and app.get both push a layer onto the same stack.
Whether a function is an error handler is decided by its arity alone (fn.length).
Express 5 catches rejected promises: an async handler that throws ends up in next(err).
No matching layer means 404 'Cannot GET /path', produced by finalhandler, not by Express.

points.title: Start in the router
points.text: Almost all of the request flow lives in Router.prototype.handle and its next(); Express only wraps it.

points.title: Layer and Route move together
points.text: The calling convention (arity checks, promise handling) is repeated in Layer.handleRequest and handleError and relied on by Route.dispatch.

points.title: The arity check is public API
points.text: Every app's error handlers are found by fn.length === 4; changing it changes which functions run on errors.

points.text: The router's own suite covers next('route'), next('router') and promise handling.
